Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Hill
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/01/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 23 as introduced provides for judicial discretion in determining the length of a revocation sentence when sentencing defendants for probation revocation under certain conditions. This could decrease the obligations of the Department of Corrections, by an undetermined amount, depending on the number of defendants that violate probation and receive a reduced revocation sentence.
Jim Hill, Chair
Judiciary

This could decrease the obligations of the Department of Corrections, by an undetermined amount, depending on the number of defendants that violate probation and receive a reduced revocation sentence.

Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Wood (R)
Analyst: Bryan Young
Date: 03/25/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 146 as passed the House of Representatives allows the Alabama Water Pollution Authority to extend the repayment period of loans issued by the Authority from 20 years currently to a period which does not exceed the expected design life of the project, if required or permitted by the Federal Clear Water Act. This could increase the total amount of interest paid by a city, county, or instrumentality thereof over the repayment period by an undetermined amount dependent upon the terms of the loan. This bill will not otherwise directly affect state or local funding.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
